evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU may elect to accept changes in Environment/Category, Identity or Exercise Indicator received in a track report with the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator set to value 1, provided the new identity is Friend and the locally held identity is not Hostile.

evidence_cards.content: A change in the ID of a given track shall include the appropriate evaluation of the Platform/Platform Activity/Specific Type and Special Interest Indicator fields, and shall be included in the J3.X or J7.0 (ACT = 1) message.

evidence_cards.content: For the automatic acceptance flow to proceed, the two tracks involved must not be of a different E/C, neither track can have an existing E/C conflict, one track cannot be simulated while the other is live, and both tracks cannot be locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These are the negative preconditions (restrictions) that must NOT hold for the automatic acceptance process to succeed; if they do hold, the correlation is rejected.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks; or (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This section defines specific constraints on the automatic correlation process (part of managing track identity), listing four distinct conditions that prevent the system from proceeding with automatic correlation, thereby acting as exceptions to the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: When the remote report being tested for correlation is a J2.0 Indirect PPLI message with the Originator E/C field set to value 0 (Surface) or 3 (Air), it shall be processed for correlation like a J3.2 air or J3.3 surface (maritime) track with TQ = 7.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a concrete processing rule within the correlation workflow, detailing how a specific type of incoming message (J2.0 Indirect PPLI) is handled during the identity classification/correlation phase.

evidence_cards.content: When conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator shall be alerted to take one of the following actions: (a) Change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation; or (b) Transmit an ID Difference Report, thereby allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the main interaction sequence for resolving identity conflicts during track correlation — a core part of managing track identity classification. It specifies the system alerting the operator and the two valid resolution paths that lead to successful automatic correlation.

evidence_cards.content: For each of the Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and Special Interest Indicator fields implemented by a C2 JU, the JU shall accept all defined field values for retransmission and operator appreciation in the event of assuming R² for a previously-reported track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system's requirement to accept identity data fields during the management process (specifically when assuming R²), which is part of the main interaction flow.

evidence_cards.content: Values accepted for retransmission shall be retransmitted if the JU assumes R², unless the JU holds locally derived data other than No Statement (non-NS) for the field which differs from the value accepted for retransmission.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the primary logic for handling identity classification data: accepting external values unless specific local data overrides them.

evidence_cards.content: If the JU holds locally derived data that differs from the accepted retransmission value, the JU shall report the locally derived data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the action taken in the main flow when local data conflicts with received data (reporting local data).

evidence_cards.content: As an exception, non-NS data for the Platform, Platform Activity, and Specific Type fields received from the controlling unit for the track shall be retransmitted regardless of locally derived data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a mandatory rule within the flow where controlling unit data takes precedence over local data for specific identity fields.

evidence_cards.content: When a JU receives a Surveillance message or a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message in which the air, surface (maritime), or land (ground) Environment/Category and ID are different from the local Environment/Category and ID, the Environment/Category conflict shall be processed and resolved prior to the resolution of the ID conflict.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary step in the main flow for handling conflicts: resolving Environment/Category differences before Identity differences.

evidence_cards.content: If an Environment/Category conflict is detected, no further processing to detect an ID conflict need occur.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies that the detection of an E/C conflict effectively pauses or bypasses immediate ID conflict detection until the E/C issue is addressed.

evidence_cards.content: Exercise Indicator conflicts will be resolved prior to ID or Identity Amplifying Descriptor Conflict resolution.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the priority order for resolving conflicts within the main flow sequence.

evidence_cards.content: Identity Amplifying Descriptor conflicts are processed in the same manner as ID conflicts.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the handling procedure for specific identity descriptors relative to standard ID conflicts.

evidence_cards.content: For the main flow of resolving Environment/Category differences: A C2 JU may elect to automatically accept changes in Environment/Category, Identity, or Exercise Indicator received in a track report with the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator set to value 1, provided the new identity is Friend and the locally held identity is not Hostile.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the automatic acceptance condition for identity classification changes, constituting the primary success scenario.

evidence_cards.content: When accepting a remote ID change (main flow), C2 JUs shall include the appropriate evaluation of the Platform/Platform Activity/Specific Type and Special Interest Indicator fields in the J3.X or J7.0 (ACT = 1) message and retain the received values of these fields for retransmission and operator appreciation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the mandatory data handling and transmission steps required when an ID change is accepted.

evidence_cards.content: The Change Data Order process (J7.0 ACT = 2) is initiated only by operator action; upon transmission, the JU rejects any received data on that track that differs for a 30-second lock-out period, except for ID data from the controlling unit.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the operator-initiated manual resolution path and its immediate system constraints (lock-out).

evidence_cards.content: If changes in data are not accepted by the controlling unit (exception/rejection path), the controlling unit shall transmit its locally held data in a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message with the Controlling Unit Indicator field set.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details the specific system response when a proposed data change is rejected during the resolution process.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it shall initiate action (automatically or manually) to resolve the dual designation by transmitting a J7.2 Correlation message requesting other C2 IUs to perform correlation, identifying the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary action in the main flow where the actor initiates the resolution process upon recognizing eligibility.

evidence_cards.content: The originating C2 JU indicates in the J7.2 message if it has any constraint which would prohibit accepting a reverse correlation using the Response Value (RV) field: value 0 indicates a reverse correlation is acceptable, value 1 indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected, value 3 indicates manual initiation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details the specific data transmission step required in the main flow to communicate constraints and initiation type.

evidence_cards.content: Receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the expected system response from receiving units in the successful interaction sequence.

evidence_cards.content: If the originating C2 JU holds R2 for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the final cleanup step in the main flow for the originating unit once the correlation is processed.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies: (1) The two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing E/C conflict; (2) One track is simulated and the other is live; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the primary success path (automatic acceptance) for the main flow when the system receives a specific correlation request (RV=3), subject to explicit blocking conditions.

evidence_cards.content: After acceptance of a manual correlation the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a post-acceptance constraint that stabilizes the track state immediately following a successful manual correlation action in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: When the Exercise Indicator is set to value 1 (Exercise Track), the standard identity of the track shall be Friend and the exercise identity shall be specified in the Identity Amplifying Descriptor field.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific step in the main flow for managing identity classification when a track is identified as an exercise track: setting the standard identity to Friend and specifying the exercise identity.

evidence_cards.content: A track with the Exercise Indicator set to value 1 and the Identity Amplifying Descriptor set to value 6 (FAKER) shall be identified as a friendly track acting as a hostile for exercise purposes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific outcome/action within the main flow for handling 'Faker' tracks during identity classification.

evidence_cards.content: A track with the Exercise Indicator set to value 1 and the Identity Amplifying Descriptor set to value 5 (JOKER) shall be identified as a friendly track acting as a suspect for exercise purposes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific outcome/action within the main flow for handling 'Joker' tracks during identity classification.

evidence_cards.content: For any track with Exercise Indicator set to value 1, data concerning the track must be considered artificial, for exercise purposes, except that the following shall not be artificial: Track Number; Tracking Data (Latitude, Longitude, Altitude/Elevation/Depth, Course, Speed, Minute, Hour, and Track Quality); Simulation Indicator; Environment/Category; Status Data on Air Tracks (Fuel Function, Fuel, Time Report Function, Minute, and Hour); and Status Data on Surface (Maritime) Tracks (Flight Deck Status, Landing/Approach Condition, and associated Time Report Function, Minute and Hour).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the system's required processing logic (considering data as artificial) and exceptions (preserving specific data fields) as part of the interaction sequence for exercise tracks.

evidence_cards.content: A track's identity can be further amplified by designating it as a track of special interest by setting the identity field as appropriate and by setting the special interest indicator.

evidence_cards.content: If either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1, C2 JUs shall not inhibit correlation; however, systems shall not inhibit correlation if either track has Strength set to No Statement.

evidence_cards.content: If the locally held Environment/Category of a track is different from the Environment/Category received in a J3.X or a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message for that track, the operator shall be alerted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception flow where a data mismatch triggers an operator alert rather than automatic resolution.

evidence_cards.content: An ID conflict exists when the ID difference cannot be automatically accepted or rejected; in this case, the differences must be presented to the operators for their evaluation and may require voice coordination for final resolution.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the exception handling path for Identity conflicts that exceed automated processing capabilities, requiring manual intervention.

evidence_cards.content: When a JU changes the Environment/Category of a track as specified above, or when a difference report is rejected by an operator action, the information shall be reported as follows: if a JU has R2, transmit local Environment/Category in Surveillance report; if no R2, transmit in J7.0 (ACT=1) message.

evidence_cards.content: When a Platform, Platform Activity or Specific Type value of 0 (No Statement) is received and a non-zero value is held locally, this constitutes an exception to the rule requiring retention of received values during remote ID change acceptance.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific condition under which the standard retention rule for platform-related fields does not apply — qualifying as an exception flow in identity classification management.

evidence_cards.content: When an Air Platform value of 6 (Tanker), 7 (Tanker (Boom Only)), or 8 (Tanker (Drogue Only)) is held locally and a different value is received, an operator alert is optional — meaning the system may proceed without alerting, constituting an exception to expected notification behavior.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a scenario where normal operator alerting expectations are waived, representing an exception path in handling tanker-type platform changes during identity resolution.

evidence_cards.content: If the Retained TN and Dropped TN decorrelate when subjected to decorrelation criteria once, the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception condition where a successful correlation attempt fails due to immediate decorrelation, resulting in rejection.

evidence_cards.content: If both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC (Operational Control Constraint), the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a constraint-based exception where dual operational constraints prevent valid correlation.

evidence_cards.content: If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is set to value 1, the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a rejection condition triggered by a specific RV field value combined with an OCC on the dropped track.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected for manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the recovery behavior (operator alert) following a rejection exception during manual correlation processing.

evidence_cards.content: Automatic acceptance of requested correlation (RV=3) is rejected if: (1) tracks are of different E/C or have existing E/C conflict; (2) one track is simulated and the other live; or (3) both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Lists specific validation failure conditions that override automatic acceptance, constituting exception paths.

evidence_cards.content: If the C2 JU receives a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message for the Dropped TN but the dropped TN is subsequently reported by another IU after that transmission, the own unit shall retain the Dropped TN as a remote track and shall not reattempt to correlate the Retained TN and the Dropped TN for a period of 60 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception flow where a correlation attempt fails due to external reporting during the drop process, resulting in a mandatory wait period rather than immediate retry.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation shall be deemed to have failed if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received for the dropped TN after a period of 60 seconds from the transmission of the correlation request, causing all associated processing for the correlation to be cancelled.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a terminal exception outcome (cancellation) triggered by a timeout condition during the execution of correlation.

evidence_cards.content: Differences in position, velocity, or altitude/elevation recognized by a JU are not resolved through conflict processing and shall not generate a J7.0 (ACT = 2) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception where specific surveillance data differences do not trigger the standard resolution flow (J7.0 ACT=2), constituting a bypass of the main conflict resolution process.

evidence_cards.content: Under the condition of automatically purging remote tracks after a specific time interval due to irregular reporting or lack of updates, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted.

evidence_cards.content: If an Environment/Category conflict is detected when a JU receives a Surveillance message or J7.0 (ACT = 1) message with differing air/surface/land classification, the C2 JU processes and resolves this conflict prior to ID conflict resolution; once detected, no further processing to detect an ID conflict occurs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific exception flow where detection of one type of conflict (Environment/Category) halts the processing of another (ID), altering the standard main flow sequence.

evidence_cards.content: When a JU receives a Surveillance message or J7.0 (ACT = 1) message in which the Exercise Indicator differs from local data, a conflict exists and the operator shall be alerted for manual resolution.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a terminal exception outcome requiring human intervention (manual resolution) rather than automatic system handling.

evidence_cards.content: If the locally held Environment/Category of a track differs from that received in a J3.X or J7.0 (ACT = 1) message, the operator shall be alerted even if the received Environment/Category is not implemented.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies an alerting requirement for exceptions involving unimplemented categories, ensuring the operator is notified despite the lack of implementation.

evidence_cards.content: If local data and received data differ regarding whether the Track Number (TN) is assigned to a point or a track, the operator shall be alerted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific exception condition regarding TN assignment logic that triggers an operator alert.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific condition under which standard data retention rules are suspended, constituting an exception flow in track identity management.

evidence_cards.content: When an Air Platform value of 6 (Tanker), 7 (Tanker (Boom Only)), or 8 (Tanker (Drogue Only)) is held locally and a different value is received, the operator alert is optional rather than mandatory.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a scenario where a potentially conflicting platform type update does not trigger a mandatory system response (alert), representing a handled exception or deviation from expected conflict resolution behavior.

evidence_cards.content: If the originating C2 JU holds R2 for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the exception flow where the correlation process triggers a subsequent track drop action based on local responsibility status.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection) shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the exception handling behavior (temporary suppression of retries) following a rejected correlation request.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the recovery path (hand-off to voice coordination) when automated correlation fails.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs rejecting the requested correlation shall initiate transmission of a J7.2 message with the Retained TN/Dropped TN set as received and RV field set to value 2.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details the system response required to formally report the rejection exception back to the network.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs responding with a reverse correlation shall transmit the J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the alternative resolution path (reverse correlation) taken when the original correlation direction is contested.

evidence_cards.content: After successful completion of track identity classification, the C2 JU has assigned a Track Number (TN) from its allocated block for each initiated and reported track/point, and holds R² responsibility for that track/point at the time of assignment.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the immediate system state after successful track initiation and reporting — specifically TN assignment and R² ownership — which are direct postconditions of managing track identity classification when it results in new or updated track reporting.

evidence_cards.content: After successful completion of managing track identity classification, the C2 JU has updated the track’s identity classification: exercise-involved live tracks are distinguished from other live tracks (via Exercise Indicator and Identity Amplifying Descriptor), Environment/Category differences are resolved, and Track Number continuity is determined per Table 4.7-1 when entity type changes.
